correctness.rationale: Connectedness forces equal three-round firing totals via the graph Laplacian. For the once-firing case the precise local interval has cardinality r_v, the number of neighbors firing on the preceding round. Choosing a predecessor neighbor by an arbitrary local order gives an exact weighted-to-functional-graph count. Every selected arrow reduces phase modulo three, hence all directed cycles have length divisible by three. Uniqueness forces a single oriented core cycle and a spanning rooted forest, counted by the multigraph contraction matrix-tree invariant. There are two orientations and three phases; bounded complement symmetry doubles the once-firing total from 6 tau to 12 tau. Independent brute-force phase/determinant enumeration passed for 4,963 unique-resonant and 3,460 zero-resonance connected labelled graphs on 3–6 vertices. Separate exhaustive update replay passed eight named graphs, including a noncactus theta graph.

value.rationale: Exact immediate-period-three census on all connected graphs with one viable three-phase feedback cycle, including noncactus theta networks; identifies a standard, independently motivated spanning-tree invariant for the entire temporal population. In cactus graphs it gives a simple multiplicative law for arbitrary attached nonresonant cycles while bridges and trees have no effect. Generalizes one-dimensional ring analysis in a structurally natural direction without requiring a downstream theorem.
